# yapmod v0.7.0

Yapmod v0.7.0 introduces a browser extension target, allowing the Yapmod client to run in Chrome and Firefox as a packaged extension. It also brings a major architectural refactor — the injected client is now multi-target, with a unified host abstraction that separates feature code from platform-specific bridges. The plugin and theme systems have grown significantly, the documentation website has been completely rebuilt, and the CI/CD pipeline has been overhauled for reliability.

### Highlights

- **Browser extension.** Yapmod can now run as a Chrome or Firefox extension. The extension loads the client behind an isolated bridge, stores plugins and themes in `chrome.storage.local`, and supports signed client updates at runtime. A separate self-hosted loader build is also available for private deployments.
- **Multi-target client architecture.** The entire client has been restructured around a unified host contract. Feature code communicates through message ports instead of direct platform calls, enabling both the desktop app and the browser extension to share the same feature logic. Desktop and web targets each implement their own host, and architecture tests enforce the boundaries.
- **Plugin UI component system.** Plugins can now build custom UI using a built-in component library with styled buttons, icons, and layout utilities. Plugins can also register custom settings panels that appear in the Yapmod settings sidebar.
- **Plugin reload.** Installed plugins and themes can now be reloaded without restarting the app. After a reload, plugins are automatically re-enabled.
- **Mono Dark and Portal community themes.** Two new community themes are available: Mono Dark, a monochrome dark theme with a subtle beige accent and custom font import, and Portal, a theme with external CSS resource support. Theme accent colors now map to Yapper's primary host CSS variables for better visual integration.
- **Quick CSS editor.** A built-in Monaco-based CSS editor lets you write and apply custom styles directly in the app, replacing the previous community plugin approach.

### Improvements and fixes

- **Settings persistence.** Settings are now backed up to `localStorage` on app close, preventing data loss when the app closes unexpectedly.
- **Plugin restore.** Plugins are properly restored after the document body exists, fixing a race condition during startup.
- **Custom settings positioning.** Custom settings panels registered by plugins now render at the bottom of the settings sidebar in the correct order.
- **Custom background opacity.** The Custom Background community plugin now supports opacity control for background images.
- **Notification and link handling.** Improved notification delivery and link opening behavior across platforms.
- **Client release fixes.** Resolved a deadlock in the client update concurrency group and a missing `OUTPUT_DIR` environment variable that could block releases.

### Development and infrastructure

- **Web extension target.** A complete browser extension shell has been added, including a page-realm bridge, extension storage backend, plugin and theme import, RPC layer, manifest, and background service worker. The extension has its own independent version (`client/targets/web/version.json`), separate from the app and client versions.
- **CI/CD pipeline overhaul.** The release workflow has been completely rewritten, consolidating seven workflow files into two. The unified release pipeline handles stable and nightly channels, desktop builds across four platforms, web extension packaging, and signed client update feed publication — all in a single workflow dispatch.
- **Unified build tooling.** A single build script now handles client bundling, type generation, and version management, replacing separate ad-hoc scripts. Web extension packaging and bundle validation are also included.
- **Documentation website rebuild.** The documentation site has been rebuilt with client-side routing, a search palette, and 22 new documentation pages covering the plugin API, theme development, architecture guides, and the web extension. API reference data is now auto-generated from the codebase.
- **Plugin and theme ecosystem.** The community plugin catalog now includes the Popup Remover plugin (contributed via PR #19). The theme catalog includes Mono Dark and Portal. Catalog infrastructure supports automatic generation and validation.
- **Simplified Rust validation.** Plugin and theme validation in the Rust backend has been simplified — the boundary is now trusted, removing duplicated policy rules. External resources (fonts, images) are allowed in plugin and theme CSS.
- **AGENTS.md.** Comprehensive AI agent guidelines have been added to help automate project maintenance and onboarding.
